title: What fractions give the lengths of the four black lines?
description: A number line from zero to two has each unit cut into five equal parts, and four black lines end at the marks between one and two. The board counts the parts from zero for each line, from six parts to nine parts, and checks that the next part would reach two.
teaching_notes: One idea: past one, the count of parts keeps growing, because one whole unit already holds five parts. Watch for students who restart the count at one.

video_script.why: A learner reads the lengths of lines longer than one unit by counting all the fifths from zero.
video_script.substitution: the book's own number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into five equal parts
video_script.anchor: the number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into five equal parts and four black lines from 0
video_script.payoff_line: The black lines are six fifths, seven fifths, eight fifths and nine fifths

final_answer.spoken: six fifths, seven fifths, eight fifths and nine fifths

video_script.fraction_reading: one fifth, six fifths, seven fifths, eight fifths, nine fifths
maths_rules: 1 unit cut into 5 equal parts: each part is 1/5 unit and the whole unit holds 5 parts
the first mark after 1 is 5 + 1 = 6 parts from 0
the next marks are 7, 8 and 9 parts from 0
check: one more part after the 9th would be the 10th part, which reaches 2
video_script.design: One number line from zero to two with five parts in each unit and four black lines that all start at zero. The count of parts is carried on past the mark one.

<bookmark mark='line'/>Each unit is cut into five equal parts, and the first four marks are labelled.
<bookmark mark='black'/>Four black lines start at zero. They end at the four marks between one and two.
Which fractions give the lengths of the black lines?

beats.on_screen: Given: each unit is cut into 5 equal parts; four black lines end at the marks between 1 and 2
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, each unit is cut into five equal parts. Four black lines end between one and two.

beats.on_screen: To find: the fractions for the lengths of the four black lines, shortest to longest
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the fractions for the four lengths, from the shortest to the longest.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 unit into 5 equal parts, each part = 1/5; 1 whole unit = 5 parts

marks.size: one part is lit and labelled 1/5
marks.holds: the first unit is marked as five parts

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step one, we use the same way as the example in your book. One unit cut into five equal parts gives one fifth each.
<bookmark mark='holds'/>The first unit holds five parts.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: shortest black line = 5 parts up to 1 + 1 more = 6 parts from 0

marks.first: the shortest black line is traced; five parts are counted up to one and one more part after it

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, the shortest line goes five parts up to one, and one more part after it. That is six parts from zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the next lines are 7, 8 and 9 parts from 0

marks.next: the other three black lines are traced and seven, eight and nine parts are counted from zero

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step three, each next line is one part longer. The lines are seven, eight and nine parts from zero.

beats.on_screen: Check: 9 parts, then 1 more part would be 10 parts, which reaches 2

marks.check: one more part is added to the longest line and its end reaches the mark two

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, add one more part to the longest line. That makes ten parts, which is two whole units.

marks.ans: the four fractions are written beside the four black lines

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The black lines are six fifths, seven fifths, eight fifths and nine fifths of a unit long.
